hypothesis: The SIC-C-c covering meta-theorem (StructuralIntelligenceMathlib.sicc_covering_meta) predicts n = c * K * log(K / delta) as the sample complexity to recover the fibration on an eps-cover of size K. On the coupon-collector realisation of eps-cover recovery in a K-cell rotational latent partition of a 2-D continuous space, the fitted constant c_fitted(K) = n_emp(K, delta) / (K * log(K / delta)) is stable to within 20% across K in {8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256} with delta = 0.05, and each n_emp meets exact recovery probability >= 1 - delta while (n_emp - 1) does not (the empirical sample count is tight).

gates.SICC_META_FITTED_C_STABLE_ACROSS_K: The range (max c_fitted - min c_fitted) divided by mean c_fitted is <= 0.20 across the six K values {8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256}. This is the sharp test: if c_fitted grows with K, the meta-theorem's constant c is not merely loose --- it has the wrong K-dependence and the composition (Theorem 6 * Theorem 5-rate) is empirically wrong for this controlled instance.
gates.SICC_META_EMPIRICAL_MEETS_TARGET: For every K in the sweep, exact inclusion-exclusion recovery probability at n_emp(K, delta) is >= 1 - delta = 0.95.
gates.SICC_META_EMPIRICAL_IS_TIGHT_BY_ONE_SAMP: For every K, exact recovery probability at (n_emp - 1) is strictly < 1 - delta, confirming the binary search returned the smallest N satisfying the target.
gates.SICC_META_ABOVE_PIGEONHOLE_FLOOR: For every K, n_emp >= K (pigeonhole on the coupon collector; recovering K distinct cells requires at least K samples).

compute.sampling: exact inclusion-exclusion on the coupon-collector recovery event; binary search for the smallest N meeting P(recovery) >= 1 - delta; no Monte Carlo
